items.description: Οι άνθρωποι αγαπούν να γελούν. Αυτός είναι ο λόγος που οι επιτυχημένοι κωμικοί βγάζουν πολλά χρήματα και γίνονται γνωστά ονόματα. Αλλά οι διάσημοι άνθρωποι δεν κρατούν όλες τις κάρτες ξεκαρδίας. Πιθανότατα όλοι γνωρίζουμε κάποιον στην καθημερινή μας ζωή με ένα δώρο για κωμικό timing. Μια από αυτές τις καθημερινές ιδιοφυΐες αυτοσχεδιασμού έπεσε πάνω στον Conan O'Brien κατά τη διάρκεια ενός επεισοδίου του SubwayTakes με τον Kareem Rahma και σ.…
items.descriptionOriginal: People love to laugh . That’s why successful comedians make big bucks and become household names. But famous folks don’t hold all the hilarity cards. We likely all know someone in our everyday lives with a gift for comedic timing. One of those everyday improv geniuses ran into Conan O’Brien during an episode of SubwayTakes with Kareem Rahma , and people are blown away by their interaction. O’Brien is known for his ability to riff off the cuff, and this woman casually went toe-to-toe with him. Her banter even had the late-night show host belly-laughing in less than a minute, and people are raving about her. Watch: @snl sign her https://t.co/nsLVxTZp7N pic.twitter.com/UzW8x8WBuy — ktoni (@chumbwumba) October 20, 2026 How the viral bit came about The premise of the show SubwayTakes is that comedian Kareem Rahma rides the New York City subway and asks riders for their “take” on a question. Most of the people he talks to are everyday New Yorkers, but celebrities also join him. In this particular episode, Conan O’Brien spent a good 20 minutes talking to Rahma about his “5 most controversial takes,” which includes things like “All statues should be made out of soap,” and “We should have a separate area for people who want to talk about their diets.” Near the end, the comedians apologize to a woman who asks to walk between them and the camera, and she says, “That’s alright, Conan,” as she sits down next to Rahma. She said it so casually that Rahma asked if O’Brien knew the woman. That’s when the riffing started, and she didn’t drop a single ball lobbed her way. Conan himself was impressed O’Brien told Rahma that he and the woman had been married, and she immediately jumped in with, “We were married a long time ago—we got two kids.” When O’Brien asked how the kids were because he hadn’t seen them in a long time, she said, “One’s in medical school, the other one’s in jail, but he’ll be home soon.” Her deadpan delivery and commitment to the bit as it went on were simply delightful, and her quick responses had everyone giggling. “You’re amazing. What’s your name?” O’Brien asked her after their interaction. She told him her name was Debbie, and he said, “You are so funny…We got a show right here. You are absolutely fantastic.” Imagine getting that kind of compliment from Conan O’Brien! Debbie told the men she owns a bar. “Have I been thrown out of it?” O’Brien asked. Without skipping a beat, she held up two fingers and said, “Twice,” which had him rolling all over again. After a recent taping of Subway Takes, a random woman sits down and proceeds to riff with Conan O’Brien matching him joke for joke by u/EchoesOfYouth in MadeMeSmile 8 tips for being funnier Commenters across social media are saying she should be on Saturday Night Live or go into improv or stand-up comedy. Maybe she will, but there are lots of Debbies in the world who are just naturally funny people with no plans to make a career out of it. Behavioral researcher Vanessa Van Edwards says being funny is also a learnable skill, and an important one at that. She suggests eight strategies for learning to be funnier: Say yes instead of no, and vice versa If the expected answer to a question is “yes,” try saying “no” instead. Unexpected responses are a big part of humor. (You can always laugh at the surprising answer that just came out of your mouth, then give your real answer, or play with it and see what happens.) 2. Play with numbers The way Debbie said she and Conan O’Brien had “two kids” and that he’d been kicked out of her bar “twice” are perfect examples of this strategy. Specificity is funny, and numbers are an easy way to be specific. 3. Use the ‘rule of 3’ The “rule of 3” in comedy refers to a pattern: normal, normal, unexpected. Van Edwards shares examples such as “I love hot dogs, hamburgers, and handsome men” and “I am so thrilled, happy, and terrified to be here!” 4. Switch characters around Again, the idea is to set up something unexpected. For example, instead of the Big Bad Wolf being the villain, treat him as the protagonist and Little Red Riding Hood as the villain. 5. Utilize ‘whatever.’ If you find yourself the butt of a joke, pull out a “Whatever” as a surprisingly powerful way to avoid getting flustered. 6. Mine your life for stories We all have funny anecdotes from our real lives, but we often don’t think of them in the moment. Keep a running list of funny stories from your life and rehearse them regularly so you can more easily pull them out. 7. Delay the funny Don’t be too eager to share that hilarious story. Save your funny bits for the right moment. 8. Craft your own unique comedy style Embrace your quirks, draw inspiration from comedians you admire, and practice until your humor comes more naturally. We may not all be as hilarious as Conan O’Brien or Debbie, but we can all bump up our humor skills to add more laughter to a world that definitely needs it. The post A random woman on the subway went toe-to-toe with Conan O’Brien. Her quick wit had him belly-laughing. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: The oceans are in trouble. Rising temperatures due to climate change not only raise sea levels but also put enormous stress on coral reefs. When waters get too warm, healthy coral will expel the helpful algae living inside them. The coral then becomes drained of color, severely weakened, and vulnerable to disease. In other words, “ bleached coral ” is dying coral. The loss of coral and coral reefs devastates vast amounts of ocean wildlife, and humans too. So finding ways to stop, slow, or reverse coral bleaching is of major interest to scientists. And the latest breakthrough was completely unintentional. Lab studying coral encounters a “happy accident” Steve Palumbi is a professor of marine sciences at Stanford and an ocean researcher. One of his major research areas is coral, and his work recently led him to notice something pretty strange in his lab. According to Science Alert, Palumbi had collected various samples from the same coral colony when two of the samples “fell” into each other inside their tank. One was bleached, or dying, and the other was completely healthy. What’s strange is that by the time he noticed the two were touching, color had begun to return to the bleached coral, specifically at the point of contact. “I was blown away watching the actual color of this healthy coral slowly spread over into this bleached coral,” Palumbi’s fellow Stanford marine scientist Danny Collins told Science Alert . The bleaching had mysteriously reversed itself. “Helping hands” method for reviving dying coral discovered The researchers were incredibly intrigued by what they were witnessing. After further study, they realized that the healthy coral—through physical contact—was actually able to pass along some of its symbiotic algae to the unhealthy coral. Testing revealed that bleached coral could make a miraculous recovery through prolonged contact with healthy coral. Crucially, direct physical contact was the key. If the pieces of coral were even a few millimeters apart, the process didn’t work. What they observed was the two corals “fusing” together and forming a “nutrient bridge” for the algae to transfer across. Just one week of contact was sufficient to build up enough good algae on the bleached coral for it to fully recover in about seven weeks. It’s like a little life-saving hug. In the wild, bleached coral can recover if environmental conditions, such as ocean temperatures, improve. But the process often takes months, which is too slow. Most coral that gets severely bleached ends up dying during that time period. The groundbreaking method and research were recently published in Science Advances . Informally, the researchers are referring to the technique as “helping hands.” Researchers temper real-world expectations Bringing healthy coral into contact with bleached coral produced amazing results in the lab, but Stanford researchers still don’t know whether the effect can be replicated in the wild. Even if it can, it’s a process that’s likely to be slow and labor-intensive, meaning “helping hands” won’t save the oceans on their own. The technique could potentially be used in emergencies to save critically endangered reefs, but the worldwide coral reef network is going to need a lot more than that to return to its full strength. Without ocean warming stopping or reversing course, coral bleaching is likely to continue and worsen. But scientists like the Stanford team are making amazing discoveries all the time that might just help us tilt the scales. The post A random lab accident just revealed the unusual technique that can revive dying coral in weeks appeared first on Upworthy .

Είναι το βράδυ που μένεις μέσα αντί να βγάλεις το σκυλί έξω για να βάλεις τα βήματά σου. «Το πρόβλημα…
items.descriptionOriginal: Most of us share a strange wiring: once we set a goal , the first setback makes it suddenly feel unachievable, and we are more likely to quit. It’s the first moment when you decide you can’t make it to the gym . It’s that first cigarette you bum after quitting. It’s the night you stay in instead of taking the dog out to get your steps in. “The problem is that these small failures really derail people,” Marissa Sharif, assistant professor of marketing at the Wharton School, said on the Ripple Effect podcast . Sharif calls the setback the “What the hell?” effect. “Basically, when we miss going to the gym one day or miss that weekly budget goal, we kind of completely abandon the goal. And the idea is, you know, ‘I failed today. There’s no way I’m going to be able to reach the goal this week. What the hell? Why would I continue?’” How to use ‘skip days’ to achieve your goals The good news is that in her research, Sharif found that if we plan for unexpected slip-ups while pursuing our goals, we’re much more likely to achieve them. To boil it down, if we slip up and miss a day at the gym, we believe we can’t achieve the goal. But if we bake some skip days into the plan, we’re more likely to pick up where we left off after we fall short. A man working out at the gym. Photo credit: Canva In her research, Sharif tested three goal options for someone whose goal is to get 10,000 steps a day: A.) Do 10,000 steps 7 days a week B.) Do 10,000 steps 5 days a week C.) Do 10,000 steps 5 days a week, with two skip days “The emergency skip version does better than both seven and five,” Sharif continued. “And that’s because people don’t want to use their emergency skips. But it also helps them if they do have to use them. So it’s kind of combining the benefits of both worlds.” Woman on a treadmill. Photo credit: Canva Skip days are the key to success A big part of it is that when you bake skip days into the plan, you feel a lot better when you miss a day, so you are less likely to give up. After all, you’re still sticking to the plan. “It kind of takes away these negative feelings about goal failure and allows people to keep going week to week to reach these bigger goals,” Sharif said. A 2021 study by Sharif and Suzanne Shu of 315 graduate students found that, over the course of a five-week study on achieving step goals, those who had “reserve conditions” or, as we call them in this piece, skip days, reached their step goals on 40% more days per week than those who did not. It’s comforting to know that none of us are perfect, and the best way to achieve a goal isn’t just white-knuckled discipline. It’s understanding that we are all human, things come up that are out of our control, and sometimes we’re just not feeling up to pushing ourselves. If you’re going to create a system to achieve big things, why not do so with a bit of grace? The post Discipline is good. But when achieving big goals, taking ‘skip days’ is just as important. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Νέα τεχνική ωθεί τα οργανικά ηλιακά κύτταρα σε απόδοση 20,4% με αντοχή 2.000 ωρών

items.descriptionOriginal: A new molecular locking strategy could help overcome the efficiency, stability, and scalability challenges in organic solar cells (OSCs). Organic solar cells offer lightweight, flexible, carbon-based alternatives to silicon and offer vast potential for commercial use. But the cells’ delicate layers typically degrade quickly under heat and continuous sunlight A team from the Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering (NIMTE) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) worked to solve this stability issue with a molecular-locking strategy that anchors the delicate solar layers together. In particular, it introduces a specialized intermediate layer that chemically anchors the solar materials to the electrodes. This structure creates strong molecular bonds for better energy efficiency and long-term durability across large-scale panels. “We achieved 20.4% small-area efficiency and 18.8% active-area module efficiency,” the study paper stated. Problem with next-gen solar cells To understand the development, you first have to understand why flexible solar cells fail. Organic solar cells (OSCs) harvest sunlight using ultrathin molecular films called self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) laid over transparent electrodes. The connection between the electrode and the organic film is slippery. Under intense heat and continuous light, the chemical bonds slide apart. The layers desorb, and the cell dies. This is a trilemma for solar cell experts: the ultimate balancing act between high efficiency, long-term stability, and commercial scalability. Up until now, optimizing for one usually meant sacrificing the others. To strengthen the troublesome solar cell interface, the NIMTE research team inserted an ultra-thin indium chloride intermediate layer that undergoes a localized reaction upon heating. This process drives out loose chlorine ions, forming a dense matrix of interconnected indium, oxygen, and phosphorus bonds. The resulting chemical network acts as a strong anchor, firmly locking the solar molecules in place rather than leaving them loosely attached. Endurance testing Heating the material triggers a chemical reaction that removes loose chlorine ions and forms strong bonds between indium, oxygen, and phosphorus. This process builds a durable protective network across the surface. The newly formed layer holds the solar cell materials tightly in place, greatly improving overall stability. “The interlayer triggers ligand exchange, forming a robust, multidentate In-O-P coordination network that densely and uniformly anchors SAMs,” the researchers noted in the press release. The strategy immediately improved performance across all key testing metrics. Small lab-scale cells reached an impressive 20.4 percent power conversion efficiency. On the other hand, larger modules with a 15.6 square centimeter area set a record efficiency of 18.8 percent. Interestingly, the devices demonstrated exceptional durability. And retained over 85% of their initial output after 2,000 hours of continuous operation under continuous illumination. “We scaled the technique to large-area modules with an aperture area of 15.6 cm2, reaching a record active-area PCE of 18.8%,” said Prof. LIU Quan, corresponding author of the study. This universal chemical-locking strategy offers a pathway for the commercial future of organic photovoltaics. Overcoming the efficiency, stability, and scalability trilemma might bring flexible solar technology much closer to mass manufacturing. One day, surfaces like skyscraper windows, car roofs, and smartwatch covers could silently generate clean electricity using these tiny chemical locks. The findings were detailed in the journal Joule on October 21.

items.description: Ένας Αμερικανός φυσικός έριξε πρόσφατα νέο φως στα μυστηριώδη σωματίδια πίσω από το Βραβείο Νόμπελ Φυσικής 2026 και εξήγησε ότι θα μπορούσαν να βοηθήσουν στην επίλυση μερικών από τα μεγαλύτερα μυστικά του σύμπαντος. Ο George Fuller, διακεκριμένος καθηγητής στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Καλιφόρνια του Σαν Ντιέγκο (UC San Diego), συνεργάστηκε με τον Francis Halzen, PhD, σε μια πρώιμη μελέτη που περιελάμβανε…
items.descriptionOriginal: A US physicist has recently shed new light on the mysterious particles behind the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics, and explained that they could help solve some of the universe’s greatest secrets. George Fuller, a distinguished professor at the University of California San Diego (UC San Diego), worked with Francis Halzen, PhD, on an early study involving the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. The Belgian-American physicist earned this year’s physics Nobel for his work on the project. Now Fuller revealed how they travel across the universe and what makes them so difficult to detect. Approximately 100 billion neutrinos pass through each square centimeter of our bodies every second. Most of them leave no trace. Fuller emphasized the importance of understanding neutrinos. “Halzen’s work, and the work of those he inspired with his vision, was foundational in giving humanity a new window on the universe and on the mysterious and notoriously slippery neutrino,” he added. Detecting ghost particles The IceCube is the world’s largest neutrino detector . Positioned in Antarctica, near the US Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station, it relies on thousands of light sensors buried in holes drilled through about 0.24 cubic miles (one cubic kilometer) of ice to detect neutrinos. The observatory was developed following Halzen’s vision in the 1990s of building a detector deep beneath Antarctica’s surface. At that depth, fewer air bubbles and impurities would interfere with measurements. But spotting these elusive particles requires extraordinary equipment since they interact so weakly with matter. As a result, the site uses a massive volume of the ice to capture signs of them. The IceCube Neutrino Laboratory at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station. Credit: Sven Lidstrom, IceCube / NSF When a high-energy neutrino hits the ice, it can release charged particles, which generate faint flashes of blue light known as Cherenkov radiation . These flashes can determine the neutrino’s energy and the direction it traveled from. Still, high-energy cosmic neutrinos are extremely rare. IceCube detects only a few dozen each year. Some have 10 billion times more energy than typical neutrinos produced by the Sun. “One detected by a similar experiment has an energy 200 times higher than that,” Fuller said. Even so, their origins remain unknown. “We don’t really know where that neutrino came from,” Fuller said. “The fact that it got here at all may be saying something profound about the universe.” Secrets of the universe As elementary particles, neutrinos can’t be broken down into smaller parts. There are three types of neutrons: electron, muon, and tau. As they rarely interact with matter, they can travel enormous distances through space at nearly the speed of light. “Neutrinos are truly ghost-like particles,” Fuller noted. “It’s hard to stop them. It’s hard to catch them. How do we even know they exist or where they are?” At the same time, their unique properties allow them to escape extreme conditions near collapsing stars and black holes. According to Fuller, neutrinos can even travel through light-years of lead without stopping, depending on their energy. Despite being so difficult to detect, these particles are incredibly abundant. Estimates suggest there are around one billion neutrinos for every atom in the cosmos. “In that sense, Halzen really is at the frontier of experimental fundamental particle physics,” the physicist concluded in a press release . New discoveries could reveal more about the Big Bang and the early universe. UC San Diego is also part of the Simons Observatory in Chile’s Atacama Desert, which studies the cosmic microwave background, the oldest light in the universe, and could also provide clues about ancient neutrinos.

Σύμφωνα με ανακοίνωση του Δήμου θέρμης, θα συνεχιστούν και την επόμενη εβδομάδα οι εκτεταμένες εργασίες στο Γυμνάσιο Βασιλικών οι οποίες ξεκίνησαν από την Δευτέρα 12 Οκτωβρίου μετά το δυσάρεστο περιστατικό με την πτώση τμήματος επιχρίσματος…
items.descriptionOriginal: Kλειστό θα είναι και την επόμενη εβδομάδα, έως την Παρασκευή 30 Οκτωβρίου το Γυμνάσιο Βασιλικών, με απόφαση του δημάρχου Θέρμης, Θεόδωρου Παπαδόπουλου. Σύμφωνα με ανακοίνωση του Δήμου θέρμης, θα συνεχιστούν και την επόμενη εβδομάδα οι εκτεταμένες εργασίες στο Γυμνάσιο Βασιλικών οι οποίες ξεκίνησαν από την Δευτέρα 12 Οκτωβρίου μετά το δυσάρεστο περιστατικό με την πτώση τμήματος επιχρίσματος (σοβά) από την οροφή της αίθουσας καλλιτεχνικών μαθημάτων που είχε ως συνέπεια τον τραυματισμό ενός μαθητή. Για προληπτικούς λόγους η διοίκηση του Δήμου αποφάσισε να προχωρήσει στο ξήλωμα του επιχρίσματος σε όλες τις αίθουσες και τους διαδρόμους του Γυμνασίου προκειμένου να αποκλειστεί κάθε ενδεχόμενο επανάληψης ανάλογου συμβάντος. «Οι εργασίες εξελίσσονται με εντατικό ρυθμό, από πολυμελή συνεργεία, ενώ συγχρόνως διενεργούνται συνεχείς έλεγχοι ώστε να εξασφαλιστεί η ασφαλής λειτουργία του σχολείου, καθώς η προστασία των μαθητών και των εκπαιδευτικών είναι ζήτημα πρώτης προτεραιότητας για τον Δήμο Θέρμης», επισημαίνεται στην ανακοίνωση. items.descriptionOriginal: Scientists have created robots the size of a pencil tip intended to travel through the body to deliver medicine to infections inside a beating heart. The bots, designed to replace risky open-heart surgery and ineffective IV-drug therapy to treat life-threatening heart infections, could also be used to less invasively and more precisely treat other hard-to-reach diseases, including cancer. “With just a little pinprick, you insert a micro robot and do a procedure without infection or blood loss. And you don’t need to have a surgeon operating it to get the drugs robustly, safely, and efficiently to the right place,” says senior author Axel Krieger, a medical roboticist known for creating robots that perform surgery without human help. “There’s a lot of areas beyond heart infections where this kind of targeted drug therapy and these kinds of steerable robots could play a major role. It’s really the frontier of surgical robotics.” The work appears in Advanced Materials Technologies . Each year about 50,000 people in the United States contract endocarditis, a heart tissue infection. The typical treatment is a weeks-long course of intravenous antibiotics, which often fails because the drugs are too diluted by the time they reach the heart. Doctors are then left with two risky choices—prescribing more and higher doses of antibiotics, which can be toxic, or extremely risky open-heart surgery. To get the drugs directly to the infected heart tissue, the team developed magnetically-powered robots called “millirobots,” because of their size—they’re as wide as a pencil tip or a matchstick head, and about as long as a grain of rice. The robots work in pairs. There’s one the team calls the needle module, which gently latches onto heart tissue right at the infected site. There it serves as a docking station, waiting right on the beating heart for the drug module. The drug module carries medicine to the docking station, where it magnetically docks and slowly releases the antibiotics right where they’re most needed. Both robots are magnetic and guided wirelessly by an external electromagnetic coil system that works like an MRI machine. Having two tiny robots instead of one larger one allows the device to reach tight spots in the body. The needle can remain docked while the drug module is replaced, allowing for repeat doses of medicine if needed. “Magnetic guidance is exciting because you don’t have to power the robot itself. It doesn’t carry batteries and motors,” Krieger says. “The drugs can be delivered safely, with technology like the gradients and fields in an MRI. But instead of using it for imaging, it drives the millirobots.” The researchers successfully tested the robots on phantom heart models that closely mimic a human heart, and on real porcine heart tissue. The robots traveled smoothly and autonomously, even against simulated blood flow. “We can just inject a robot with a little pill into your vein where it travels to the site, right to where we really need to deliver the drugs, and it’s minimally invasive,” says first author Anuruddha Bhattacharjee, a former Johns Hopkins postdoctoral student who is now an assistant professor at the University of Alabama at Birmingham. In addition to eliminating the need for open-heart surgery, drug treatment with the robots could take hours instead of weeks. “Usually if you do IV drug treatment, you need four to six weeks of therapy. But with these robots the entire procedure might take 10 minutes—maybe an hour if you want to do a couple rounds,” Bhattacharjee says. “If everything works well, you go from four to six weeks of treatment to one day or less.” The team also believes the robots would be helpful delivering targeted medications to fight cancer where it’s spreading. The researchers next plan to test the robots in more realistic phantom hearts, with muscle contraction and the beating movement of a real heart. The work was supported by the National Science Foundation’s Foundational Research in Robotics CAREER program. Additional authors are from Johns Hopkins, the University of Maryland, and Weinberg Medical Physics. Source: Johns Hopkins University The post Could tiny robots replace open-heart surgery? appeared first on Futurity .

items.descriptionOriginal: Researchers at the University of Arkansas and the University of Michigan have reported the creation of a graphene-based energy harvester that uses ambient radiation to run ultralow-power temperature sensors. This is the second sensor created by the team whose overall goal is development of autonomous sensor systems that draw power from multiple sources in the environment—solar, thermal, acoustic, kinetic, nonlinear and ambient radiation. The findings are published in the Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B.

items.descriptionOriginal: At 74, she decided to learn something new. Today, at 82, she rides a bike, drives a tractor and shares her adventures on social media! Sukhma’s journey began when a joke turned into a secret learning adventure between her and a family member. Away from the rest of the family, they practised together until she finally learnt to ride. Eight years later, she’s doing much more than riding a bike. She drives a tractor and runs her own social media page, sharing reels of herself riding. She didn’t learn because she had to. She learnt because she wanted to. Sukhma’s story reminds us that curiosity has no expiry date, and age doesn’t have to stop us from trying something we’ve always wanted to do. If you could learn anything new at 74, what would it be? #AgeIsJustANumber #InspiringWomen #WomenWhoInspire #NeverTooLate #TheBetterIndia Subscribe Us Now : https://www.youtube.com/thebetterindia Follow us for more: Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/thebetterindia Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/thebetterindia/ Twitter: https://twitter.com/thebetterindia LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/thebetterindia/ Website: https://www.thebetterindia.com/

Το έργο του κορυφαίου εκπροσώπου του ιμπρεσιονισμού δημοπρατήθηκε στις 22 Οκτωβρίου 2026, με την τελική τιμή να υπερβαίνει σημαντικά την αρχική εκτίμηση του οίκου δημοπρασιών, η οποία…
items.descriptionOriginal: Έναντι 50 εκατομμυρίων ευρώ, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των προμηθειών του αγοραστή, πωλήθηκε στο Παρίσι ο πίνακας «Ίρις» του Κλοντ Μονέ, καταγράφοντας νέο ρεκόρ για έργο τέχνης που διατίθεται σε δημοπρασία στη Γαλλία. Το έργο του κορυφαίου εκπροσώπου του ιμπρεσιονισμού δημοπρατήθηκε στις 22 Οκτωβρίου 2026, με την τελική τιμή να υπερβαίνει σημαντικά την αρχική εκτίμηση του οίκου δημοπρασιών, η οποία κυμαινόταν μεταξύ 22 και 30 εκατομμυρίων ευρώ. Ένα έργο που παρέμενε κρυμμένο από τα βλέμματα του κοινού Ο πίνακας, ύψους 1,60 μέτρων και πλάτους 1,80 μέτρων, αποτελούσε μέρος της συλλογής της οικογένειας Σλumberger και παρέμενε στην παρισινή κατοικία της για δεκαετίες. Σύμφωνα με το AFP, δεν είχε απομακρυνθεί ποτέ από το σπίτι της οικογένειας, ενώ μέχρι πρόσφατα ήταν γνωστός μόνο μέσα από μια ασπρόμαυρη φωτογραφία. Διαβάστε ακόμα Το έργο είχε αποκτήσει η Ζαν Σλumberger, σύμφωνα με τον Τομά Μπομπάρ, εκπρόσωπο του οίκου Sotheby’s στη Γαλλία. Η περιορισμένη δημόσια παρουσία του πίνακα συνέβαλε στο ενδιαφέρον γύρω από τη δημοπρασία, καθώς επρόκειτο για ένα έργο που παρέμενε μακριά από τη διεθνή αγορά τέχνης. The Paris Sales kicked off with new records set and white-glove results for The Schlumberger Collection. Watch auctioneer Aurélie Vandevoorde drop the final hammer on this historic sale. All lots sold from this collection of unseen Modern and Impressionist masterpieces. It totaled €74.4 million, making it the most valuable fine art sale ever held at #SothebysParis. The evening was led by Claude Monet’s ‘Iris,’ which sold for €50 million and became the most valuable artwork sold at auction in France. Other highlights include a lush garden painting by Pierre Bonnard, a celebrated cast from Camille Claudel, and three more Monet masterworks. The Paris Sales continue tomorrow with Surrealism and Its Legacy and Modernités. Register to bid at the link in bio. — Sotheby’s (@Sothebys) October 22, 2026 Νέο ορόσημο για την αγορά τέχνης στη Γαλλία Η πώληση του «Ίρις» επιβεβαιώνει τη δυναμική που εξακολουθούν να διατηρούν τα έργα των μεγάλων δημιουργών του ιμπρεσιονισμού στη διεθνή αγορά. Η τελική τιμή των 50 εκατομμυρίων ευρώ ξεπέρασε κατά πολύ το ανώτατο όριο της αρχικής εκτίμησης και ανέδειξε το έργο σε μία από τις σημαντικότερες δημοπρατικές πωλήσεις στη χώρα. Ο Κλοντ Μονέ, κεντρική μορφή του ιμπρεσιονισμού, εξακολουθεί να προσελκύει το ενδιαφέρον συλλεκτών και επενδυτών, με έργα του να διεκδικούνται σε δημοπρασίες υψηλού οικονομικού ανταγωνισμού. Διαβάστε ακόμα Διαβάστε ακόμα Πηγή: AFP The post Ιστορικό ρεκόρ για τον πίνακα «Ίρις» του Μονέ: Πουλήθηκε 50 εκατ. ευρώ σε δημοπρασία appeared first on POPAGANDA .

items.descriptionOriginal: An unpublished, undated manuscript belonging to Erwin Schrödinger lies in the Austrian Central Library for Physics at the University of Vienna. Physicist Flavio Del Santo at the University of Geneva retrieved it and analyzed its contents to establish a likely date it was written and also what the famous physicist thought about random outcomes in quantum physics. The draft is titled ‘Collapse of Determinism’ and addresses one of the major problems in quantum physics – randomness of events. Quantum theory is usually used to predict the probabilities of measurement but never specific outcomes. Physicists have wondered whether this is a result of incomplete knowledge of the domain. For instance, the outcome of a coin toss seems random at first. However, if one has information about how hard the coin was tossed and the speed of the wind in the area of the toss, then there is reliable information to predict the outcome too. In the quantum realm, much remains uncertain. However, if particles carry information that determines their behavior, would they become more predictable or deterministic? What famous physicists thought The debate between determinism and indeterminism in quantum mechanics has split the physicists into two groups that stand strongly by their views. While Einstein, David Bohm, and Schrödinger are often seen as champions of determinism in scientific history, Santo argues that there stance was more nuanced and less polarised than many think. Schrödinger’s unpublished manuscript is a case in point. Quantum particles carrying information that could determine their behavior is termed hidden variables, since this information might not be accessible for scientists to observe it. In 1932, mathematician John von Neumann published a result that suggested that hidden variables should not be added to quantum mechanics, During World War II, Taylor Whittaker, a British physicist and mathematician, questioned determinism, invoking Neurman’s work and citing an example of polarized light passing through a polarizer. In this setup, the angle between the polarized light and the polarizer determines how much light can pass through the latter. Quantum mechanics expresses the outcome as a probability. However, Whittaker used two values for hidden variables in this hypothesis and argued that these could not reproduce the changes that were created when the polarizer was turned. Schrondinger’s manuscript is a response to this assumption. What Schrödinger wrote In his three-page manuscript, Schrondinger questions the restriction built into Whittaker’s reasoning and wonders why hidden variables had only two possible values. Instead, he suggested an alternative where each photon was assigned a value between zero and one. The numbers were distributed evenly across the incoming beam, and whether the photon passed the polarizer depended on its number and the polarizer’s angle. Across photons, the setup reproduced the expected transmission rate, which can be predicted using Malus’ law, but each individual outcome depended on the apparatus setting and the proposed number of the photon. Schrodinger’s manuscript also solves the problem that arises after the first measurement, where the distribution changes. So, he created a mathematical rule that changes the photon’s number after it is transmitted or reflected and restores the distribution as per Malus’ law. The question then remains is why did Schrödinger not publish this? According to Del Santo, this was likely because Heinrich Pelzer, an Austrian physicist, challenged Whittaker in a published paper. Although Pelzer’s approach was different, it still made the same point. Del Santo warns that the manuscript must not be used to claim that Schrondinger sided with a deterministic view of nature. This unpublished work could be a test of an argument rather than endorse the model, Del Santo wrote in a analysis paper. This paper can be found on the preprint server arXiv .

items.descriptionOriginal: Search any grocery store for protein-rich food that’s good for both you and the planet, and you’re buffeted by certified labels claiming organic-grown, ocean-friendly, low-carbon, fair trade, free range, or other shining attributes. These well-meaning labels can obscure serious tradeoffs—for example healthy tree nuts that minimize greenhouse emissions while guzzling scarce water, or organic meats and cheeses that spew water pollution or planet-warming gases. A health tech scientist has proposed a new solution to this problem , in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems . The paper sketches a new rating system for high-protein foods that encompasses multiple dimensions of environmental, health, and human impacts—calculating simple overall scores that can be compared across a variety of plant- and animal-derived foods. “The goal is not necessarily to create another front-of-package label, but to foster a new literacy” that enables better-informed decision-making, writes Chris Macdonald of the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom. Maintaining sufficient dietary protein is a major concern when it comes to reconciling modern agriculture with future climate change. Scientists have spent years searching for new, non-meat protein sources , ranging from marigold flowers to fungi to alternative cropping schemes . But currently available non-meat foods are also high in protein, and Macdonald has found that misunderstandings about protein content are a major factor preventing people from choosing these the most climate-intensive diet? In his latest research, Macdonald is trying to provide people with information that is accurate, comprehensive, and simple, so they can make good choices on dietary proteins. He mined scientific data on the environmental impacts and nutrient contents of various foods to develop two simple ratings. A Planet Score, ranging from 0 to 16, includes measures of greenhouse emissions, water pollution, water use, and land use per hundred grams of protein. A separate People Score, ranging from 0 to 24, includes measures of cholesterol, saturated fat, sodium, essential amino acids, commercial availability, and affordability. The Planet and People scores are then combined into an overall Better Proteins Institute (BPI) score. When Macdonald applied the system to 20 foods (10 animal and 10 plant) , tofu, chia seeds, beans, and quinoa had the highest scores (30 to 36), while cheddar, mozzarella, lamb chops, and beef steak had the lowest scores (13 to 16). The highest-scoring animal foods were chicken breast and tuna, ranking 7th and 8th out of 20, based largely on their affordability, low saturated fats, low land use, and moderate greenhouse emissions. Walnuts and brazil nuts were the lowest-scoring plant foods, ranking 11th and 12th out of 20, due to their high prices, saturated fats, and water use. Macdonald views this as a starting point, which he hopes to improve over time. Affordability and commercial availability, for example, were determined within the U.K. for this study—but they will vary substantially between regions. Future versions may also contain additional factors such as fair trade, ethical treatment of workers, or animal treatment. Macdonald. “ What are the best sources of protein? Introducing the BPI score .” Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems , 2026. image: ©Anthropocene Magazine

items.descriptionOriginal: Νέες εξελίξεις στην υπόθεση του ιατρείου της Μαρίας Καρυστιανού στη Θεσσαλονίκη, μετά τη γνωμοδότηση του Κεντρικού Συμβουλίου Υγείας (ΚΕΣΥ) για τα μηχανήματα βιοσυντονισμού και τις αναφορές στην αποκαλούμενη «κβαντική ιατρική». Όπως δήλωσε ο πρόεδρος του Ιατρικού Συλλόγου Θεσσαλονίκης , Νίκος Μπάτζιος, η απάντηση του ΚΕΣΥ αναφέρει ότι τα επίμαχα μηχανήματα δεν θα έπρεπε να βρίσκονται στο ιατρείο της Μαρίας Καρυστιανού, ενώ πλέον θα εξεταστεί εάν συντρέχει λόγος παραπομπής της σε πειθαρχικό έλεγχο. Μιλώντας στον ραδιοφωνικό σταθμό Status 107,7 και στη δημοσιογράφο Έφη Παφίτου, ο κ. Μπάτζιος εξήγησε ότι ο Ιατρικός Σύλλογος ανέμενε μια συνολική τοποθέτηση του ΚΕΣΥ για τα ζητήματα που είχε θέσει σχετικά με τη λειτουργία του συγκεκριμένου ιατρείου. «Αναμέναμε μια συνολική απάντηση για όλα τα θέματα που θέσαμε στο ΚΕΣΥ, η οποία ήρθε σήμερα και λέει ότι τα επίμαχα μηχανήματα που διαθέτει στο ιατρείο της η κ. Καρυστιανού δεν θα έπρεπε να βρίσκονται εκεί», ανέφερε χαρακτηριστικά. Πώς θα αποφασιστεί εάν θα υπάρξει πειθαρχική παραπομπή Ο πρόεδρος του Ιατρικού Συλλόγου Θεσσαλονίκης περιέγραψε αναλυτικά τα επόμενα βήματα, διευκρινίζοντας ότι η γνωμοδότηση δεν συνεπάγεται αυτομάτως την επιβολή κάποιας πειθαρχικής κύρωσης. Αρχικά, η αρμόδια επιτροπή ελέγχου των ιατρείων θα εξετάσει το περιεχόμενο της γνωμοδότησης. Εφόσον κριθεί απαραίτητο, θα ζητηθούν γραπτές εξηγήσεις από τη Μαρία Καρυστιανού, προτού διαβιβαστεί σχετική εισήγηση στο διοικητικό συμβούλιο του Συλλόγου. «Θα ακολουθηθεί μια συγκεκριμένη διαδικασία. Θα πρέπει να λάβει γνώση της γνωμοδότησης του ΚΕΣΥ η επιτροπή που ελέγχει τα ιατρεία. Εάν δεν καλύπτεται, θα πρέπει να ζητήσει εγγράφως εξηγήσεις από την κ. Καρυστιανού ή όποιον άλλο γιατρό αφορά. Αφού δει τις εξηγήσεις, εισηγείται στο διοικητικό συμβούλιο και εκείνο αποφασίζει αν θα πρέπει να πάει ο ελεγχόμενος γιατρός στο πειθαρχικό ή όχι», εξήγησε. «Δεν υπάρχει κβαντική ή ολιστική ιατρική» Ιδιαίτερη αναφορά έκανε ο κ. Μπάτζιος στους όρους «κβαντική ιατρική» και «ολιστική ιατρική», επισημαίνοντας ότι, σύμφωνα με τη γνωμοδότηση του ΚΕΣΥ, δεν αναγνωρίζονται ως ιατρικές ειδικότητες. «Το ΚΕΣΥ λέει ότι δεν υπάρχει κβαντική ή ολιστική ιατρική και σας διαβεβαιώνω ότι δεν είναι κανένας γιατρός εγγεγραμμένος στον Ιατρικό Σύλλογο Θεσσαλονίκης ως κβαντικός», υπογράμμισε. Παράλληλα, αποκάλυψε ότι έχει ήδη ζητηθεί από τη Μαρία Καρυστιανού να μη χρησιμοποιούνται τα συγκεκριμένα μηχανήματα. «Ήδη έχει ζητηθεί από την κ. Καρυστιανού να μην λειτουργούν τα συγκεκριμένα μηχανήματα και η ίδια έχει δηλώσει ότι αυτά βρίσκονται εκτός λειτουργίας» , σημείωσε. Τι υποστηρίζει η δικηγόρος της Μαρίας Καρυστιανού Από την πλευρά της, η δικηγόρος της Μαρίας Καρυστιανού, Μαρία Γρατσία, αμφισβητεί τη νέα γνωμοδότηση του ΚΕΣΥ, επικαλούμενη παλαιότερη απόφαση του ίδιου φορέα. Σύμφωνα με όσα ανέφερε σε συνέντευξή της, η απόφαση που εκδόθηκε στις 6 Οκτωβρίου 2026 ουσιαστικά ανατρέπει προηγούμενη τοποθέτηση του ΚΕΣΥ σχετικά με τον βιοσυντονισμό και τη βιοανάδραση. Η κ. Γρατσία υποστηρίζει ότι το προηγούμενο πλαίσιο, σε συνδυασμό με τους σχετικούς Κωδικούς Αριθμούς Δραστηριότητας (ΚΑΔ) και τη νομοθεσία που επικαλείται, επέτρεπε τη χρήση των συγκεκριμένων μεθόδων. Απαντώντας στις σχετικές αιτιάσεις, ο πρόεδρος του Ιατρικού Συλλόγου Θεσσαλονίκης ξεκαθάρισε ότι ο Σύλλογος δεν συμμετείχε στη διαμόρφωση της γνωμοδότησης του ΚΕΣΥ, αλλά προσέφυγε στον αρμόδιο επιστημονικό φορέα προκειμένου να υπάρξει επίσημη απάντηση. «Ο Ιατρικός Σύλλογος Θεσσαλονίκης δεν έχει καμία σχέση με αυτή την απόφαση. Εμείς ακολουθήσαμε τη νόμιμη οδό γιατί ακριβώς δεν θέλουμε να είναι αμφισβητήσιμος ο οποιοσδήποτε έλεγχός μας», κατέληξε ο κ. Μπάτζιος. Η υπόθεση βρίσκεται πλέον στο στάδιο αξιολόγησης της γνωμοδότησης από τα αρμόδια όργανα του Ιατρικού Συλλόγου, τα οποία θα κρίνουν εάν απαιτούνται περαιτέρω εξηγήσεις και αν υπάρχει λόγος να κινηθεί πειθαρχική διαδικασία. Ειδήσεις σήμερα 50 φοιτητές της Ιατρικής Σχολής ΕΚΠΑ στο Ωνάσειο Νοσοκομείο Εκδήλωση της ΕΑΕ για τον γυναικείο μαστό μέσα από την τέχνη Οι νοσηλευτές καταγγέλλουν τον αποκλεισμό τους από τη συζήτηση νομοσχεδίου στη Βουλή

items.descriptionOriginal: Πενήντα φοιτητές της Ιατρικής Σχολής του Εθνικού και Καποδιστριακού Πανεπιστημίου Αθηνών επισκέφθηκαν για δεύτερη συνεχόμενη χρονιά το Ωνάσειο Νοσοκομείο, έχοντας την ευκαιρία να γνωρίσουν από κοντά τις σύγχρονες υποδομές του και να ενημερωθούν για το κλινικό και επιστημονικό του έργο. Η εκπαιδευτική επίσκεψη διοργανώθηκε από τον Παναγιώτη Στάμο, τελειόφοιτο φοιτητή της Ιατρικής Σχολής του ΕΚΠΑ, και συγκέντρωσε φοιτητές από όλα τα έτη σπουδών. Κατά τη διάρκεια της περιήγησής τους στα τμήματα του Νοσοκομείου, οι φοιτητές ενημερώθηκαν για την οργάνωση και τη λειτουργία τους, εκφράζοντας ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον για τις εξελίξεις στη σύγχρονη καρδιολογία και τις μεταμοσχεύσεις. Παράλληλα, είχαν την ευκαιρία να συζητήσουν με τους ανθρώπους του Ωνασείου για τις σύγχρονες κλινικές πρακτικές και τις δυνατότητες που προσφέρει η εξέλιξη της ιατρικής επιστήμης. Στην επίσκεψη συμμετείχε ο Πρόεδρος του Ωνασείου Νοσοκομείου, καθηγητής Ιωάννης Μπολέτης, ο οποίος συνομίλησε με τους φοιτητές και μοιράστηκε μαζί τους την εμπειρία του από την κλινική πράξη και τις εξελίξεις στην ιατρική. «Η επαφή των φοιτητών με ένα σύγχρονο νοσοκομειακό περιβάλλον είναι πολύτιμη για την εκπαιδευτική τους πορεία. Στο Ωνάσειο Νοσοκομείο, η επιστημονική γνώση και η κλινική εμπειρία βρίσκονται καθημερινά σε στενή σύνδεση. Είναι χαρά μας να υποδεχόμαστε νέους ανθρώπους που επιλέγουν την ιατρική και να τους δίνουμε την ευκαιρία να γνωρίσουν από κοντά το έργο μας. Η συνέχιση της πρωτοβουλίας αυτής για δεύτερη χρονιά αναδεικνύει τη σημασία της συνεργασίας με την ακαδημαϊκή κοινότητα», δήλωσε ο καθηγητής Ιωάννης Μπολέτης. Η επίσκεψη αναδεικνύει τη σημασία της σύνδεσης της ιατρικής εκπαίδευσης με την κλινική πράξη, προσφέροντας στους μελλοντικούς γιατρούς τη δυνατότητα να εξοικειωθούν με τις σύγχρονες εξελίξεις στην καρδιολογία, τις μεταμοσχεύσεις και τη νοσοκομειακή περίθαλψη. Ειδήσεις σήμερα ΔΕΠΥ στην ενήλικη ζωή – Πότε χρειάζεται να δούμε ειδικό για τις δυσκολίες οργάνωσης και συγκέντρωσης Κανείς μόνος απέναντι στον καρκίνο: Η δύναμη της φροντίδας πέρα από τη θεραπεία Το συχνό περπάτημα πριν από ένα χειρουργείο προφυλάσσει από επιπλοκές

items.titleOriginal: Εκδήλωση της ΕΑΕ για τον γυναικείο μαστό μέσα από την τέχνη
items.description: Ο γυναικείος μαστός αποτελεί διαχρονικά πηγή καλλιτεχνικής έμπνευσης, αλλά κι ένα ισχυρό σύμβολο της γυναικείας ταυτότητας και της ανθρώπινης εμπειρίας. Αυτή τη σχέση ανάμεσα στο σώμα, την τέχνη και την υγεία επιχειρεί να αναδείξει η Ελληνική Αντικαρκινική Εταιρεία (ΕΑΕ), μέσα από την εκδήλωση «Ο γυναικείος μαστός μέσα από την τέχνη» . Η εκδήλωση θα πραγματοποιηθεί την Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου…
items.descriptionOriginal: Ο γυναικείος μαστός αποτελεί διαχρονικά πηγή καλλιτεχνικής έμπνευσης, αλλά κι ένα ισχυρό σύμβολο της γυναικείας ταυτότητας και της ανθρώπινης εμπειρίας. Αυτή τη σχέση ανάμεσα στο σώμα, την τέχνη και την υγεία επιχειρεί να αναδείξει η Ελληνική Αντικαρκινική Εταιρεία (ΕΑΕ), μέσα από την εκδήλωση «Ο γυναικείος μαστός μέσα από την τέχνη» . Η εκδήλωση θα πραγματοποιηθεί την Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου 2026, στις 18:30, στο Ίδρυμα Β. & Μ. Θεοχαράκη, με στόχο να φέρει την τέχνη και την επιστήμη σ’ έναν κοινό διάλογο. Σύμφωνα με την ανακοίνωση της ΕΑΕ, η πρωτοβουλία επιδιώκει να φωτίσει τις διαφορετικές όψεις της σχέσης του γυναικείου σώματος με τον πολιτισμό και την κοινωνία, αναδεικνύοντας παράλληλα ζητήματα που συνδέονται με την υγεία και την ποιότητα ζωής των γυναικών. Η τέχνη ως αφετηρία για την ενημέρωση και την πρόληψη Πέρα από την καλλιτεχνική της διάσταση, η εκδήλωση έχει και έναν ουσιαστικό στόχο δημόσιας υγείας: την ενίσχυση της ευαισθητοποίησης για την πρόληψη και την έγκαιρη διάγνωση του καρκίνου του μαστού . Όπως επισημαίνει η Ελληνική Αντικαρκινική Εταιρεία, η αξιοποίηση της τέχνης και του πολιτισμού μπορεί να αποτελέσει έναν διαφορετικό τρόπο προσέγγισης θεμάτων υγείας, ενθαρρύνοντας την ενημέρωση, την ευαισθησία και την κοινωνική αλληλεγγύη. Η συγκεκριμένη πρωτοβουλία εντάσσεται στις δράσεις της Εταιρείας για την ανάδειξη της σημασίας της πρόληψης και την ενίσχυση της γνώσης γύρω από τον καρκίνο. Πανελλαδική εκστρατεία κατά του στιγματισμού Παράλληλα με την εκδήλωση, η Ελληνική Αντικαρκινική Εταιρεία ανακοινώνει την έναρξη πανελλαδικής εκστρατείας ενημέρωσης, με επίκεντρο τις σημαντικές προόδους που έχουν σημειωθεί στην επιβίωση των γυναικών που έχουν διαγνωστεί με καρκίνο του μαστού. Σύμφωνα με την ΕΑΕ, η εξέλιξη αυτή καθιστά ακόμη πιο επιτακτική την ανάγκη να αντιμετωπιστεί ο κοινωνικός στιγματισμός που μπορεί να συνοδεύει μια διάγνωση καρκίνου. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στην ανάγκη να μην προσδιορίζονται διαρκώς οι άνθρωποι που έχουν νοσήσει από την ταμπέλα του «καρκινοπαθούς», αλλά να αναγνωρίζονται πέρα από την εμπειρία της ασθένειας. Με αυτή την πρωτοβουλία, η Εταιρεία επιδιώκει να συμβάλει σε μια αλλαγή της κοινωνικής αντίληψης για τον καρκίνο, συνδέοντας την πρόοδο της ιατρικής με τον σεβασμό στην αξιοπρέπεια και την ποιότητα ζωής των ανθρώπων που έχουν βιώσει τη νόσο. Πότε και πού θα πραγματοποιηθεί η εκδήλωση Η εκδήλωση «Ο γυναικείος μαστός μέσα από την τέχνη», που διοργανώνει η Ελληνική Αντικαρκινική Εταιρεία, θα πραγματοποιηθεί την Παρασκευή 23 Οκτωβρίου 2026, στις 18:30, στο Ίδρυμα Β. & Μ. Θεοχαράκη, στην Αθήνα. Διαβάστε επίσης Πώς μπορούμε να «προλάβουμε» τον καρκίνο μαστού – Τι ρόλο παίζουν γονίδια, στρες και τρόπος ζωής Καρκίνος μαστού: Οι θεραπείες που αλλάζουν την πρόγνωση Καρκίνος μαστού: Οι αλλαγές που δεν πρέπει να αγνοούμε – Πότε ξεκινά ο έλεγχος

Τα βακτήρια διαβρώνουν τα εμφυτεύματα τιτανίου, απελευθερώνοντας μικροσκοπικά σωματίδια που καταλαμβάνουν τα κύτταρα του ανοσοποιητικού συστήματος, προκαλούν καταστροφική φλεγμονή και επιταχύνουν την απώλεια οστού της γνάθου.
items.descriptionOriginal: Researchers have uncovered a surprising reason dental implant infections often resist antibiotics: the implants themselves can contribute to the problem. Bacteria corrode titanium implants, releasing microscopic particles that hijack immune cells, trigger destructive inflammation, and accelerate jawbone loss.

Οι ερευνητές πιστεύουν ότι η τεχνολογία θα μπορούσε να μεταμορφώσει τη φροντίδα του PTSD και να ανοίξει το δρόμο για πιο ακριβείς θεραπείες για άλλες καταστάσεις ψυχικής υγείας.
items.descriptionOriginal: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

Από τα αντικείμενα στο σπίτι σας μέχρι τα συστήματα γύρω σας, αναλύουμε τις ιδέες πίσω από αυτά σε απλό, κατανοητό lan…
items.descriptionOriginal: This story is part of "How Does It Work?" — The Better India's series that takes the everyday things you see, use and rely on, and uncovers the clever technology, design and sustainable thinking that makes them work better. From the objects in your home to the systems around you, we break down the ideas behind them in simple, easy-to-understand language. Because innovation isn't always about futuristic machines or complicated technology. Sometimes, it's hiding in the things we use every day. Look at a satellite image of a cyclone, and you will see enormous bands of clouds spiralling over the ocean. What looks like a swirling mass of white clouds is actually a complex weather system, powered by warm seawater and shaped by winds moving thousands of metres above the Earth. Predicting where this storm will travel, how strong it will become, and whether it will make landfall is no small feat. Yet, today, satellites and artificial intelligence (AI) are helping scientists make these forecasts faster and more accurately, giving communities valuable time to prepare. In India, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) uses satellites such as INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR to monitor cyclones. In 2025, satellite imagery helped track weather systems, including Cyclone Montha, which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm. But how do machines in space and AI models on Earth work together to forecast a storm that has not yet reached the coast? Step 1: Satellites keep an eye on the ocean The first step is observation. Geostationary weather satellites orbit approximately 36,000 km above the equator, moving at the same rate as the Earth's rotation. This allows them to continuously observe the same broad region, capturing changes in cloud formations and atmospheric conditions. India's INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR satellites monitor clouds, atmospheric moisture and temperatures to track developing storms. Photograph: ( The Week ) India's INSAT satellites use specialised sensors to capture visible-light and infrared images, as well as information about water vapour in the atmosphere. Unlike ordinary cameras, infrared sensors can measure temperatures even at night, helping scientists identify the cold, high cloud tops associated with powerful thunderstorms. Scientists look for clues such as clusters of thunderstorms, curved cloud bands and the beginnings of a rotating system. Other satellite instruments measure ocean temperatures, rainfall and wind-related conditions, helping meteorologists understand whether the environment is becoming favourable for a cyclone. Think of it as watching a storm's earliest movements from above, even when it is far out at sea and beyond the view of coastal observers. Step 2: AI learns to recognise weather patterns Collecting data is only half the job. Scientists must also work out what it means for the storm's future. This is where AI comes in. AI weather models are trained using decades of historical weather observations , atmospheric measurements and records of past storms. By studying these examples, they learn relationships between variables such as wind speed, air pressure, humidity and temperature. For instance, a model may learn that certain combinations of atmospheric conditions and ocean temperatures have previously been associated with a storm strengthening or changing direction. AI models analyse historical weather data to learn patterns in wind, pressure and temperature. Photograph: ( CNET ) It is a little like learning to recognise a familiar pattern in a jigsaw puzzle. The AI compares the current conditions with patterns it has learnt, then estimates how the weather could evolve. Google DeepMind's WeatherNext Cyclones is one example. Its model combines global weather information with historical cyclone records to forecast a storm's path, intensity and wind structure. In 2025, its forecasts helped the US National Hurricane Center anticipate Hurricane Melissa's rapid intensification and landfall in Jamaica. Step 3: The AI runs multiple possible futures Here is where the technology becomes particularly useful. Weather is a constantly changing system. A small difference in wind direction or atmospheric pressure can alter a cyclone's eventual path . So, instead of treating one prediction as certain, advanced AI models can generate multiple possible scenarios. This technique is called ensemble forecasting . Imagine a cyclone moving towards the eastern coast of India. One forecast might show it turning north, another might suggest it moving towards the northwest, while others may predict different speeds or intensities. Ensemble forecasting generates multiple possible storm tracks, helping meteorologists assess uncertainty. Photograph: ( FOX Weather ) By comparing these possible tracks, meteorologists can identify areas that are more likely to be affected and understand where uncertainty remains. WeatherNext Cyclones can generate 1,000 possible scenarios in less than a minute on specialised computing hardware. Its forecasts can extend up to 15 days ahead, although uncertainty generally increases the further into the future a prediction looks. Step 4: Forecasters turn predictions into warnings AI does not replace meteorologists. Instead, its predictions complement satellite observations, conventional weather models and expert analysis. Forecasters assess the available evidence before issuing official warnings about a cyclone's likely track, strength, rainfall and landfall. These warnings help authorities plan evacuations, fishermen return to shore, and emergency teams prepare shelters and supplies. The goal is not to predict every movement perfectly. It is to reduce uncertainty early enough for people to act. Early warnings help coastal communities prepare, fishermen return to shore and authorities organise evacuations. Photograph: ( facebook/@TheMech Mind) As satellites collect more detailed observations and AI models become better at interpreting them, cyclone forecasting continues to improve. Every additional hour of reliable warning can give vulnerable communities more time to protect homes, secure essential supplies and move to safety. A cyclone may be impossible to control, but understanding its likely path is becoming easier. And that growing ability to see a storm coming is one of the most important ways technology can help save lives. Sources: 'Cyclone Track Forecasting Based on Satellite Images Using Artificial Neural Networks' by Rita Kovord nyi and Chandan Roy. 'How Satellites Track Hurricanes' by National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service 'How we're supporting better tropical cyclone prediction with AI' by Google Deep Mind.

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Provincial Tree Pageant Reminds Communities to Honour Their Big Trees Reading Time: 2 minutes Ontario’s Tree Trust celebrates a rare, century-old Cucumber Tree in St. George, honoring one family’s decades of stewardship and the community’s growing love for mature trees. In recent years, the Ontario government has significantly reduced environmental protection legislation. Increased development with minimal consequences threatens the province’s biodiversity, habitat, and once-protected natural character. But people are fighting back. Despite the current lack of legislation, environmental communities continue to raise awareness and push their cause. Tree Trust , a not-for-profit, grassroots organization that focuses on mature tree protection, is one of them. Education, advocacy, and community engagement are Tree Trust’s core values. Based in Elora, Tree Trust launched in 2019 and now extends to 12 communities, with chapters run entirely by volunteers. In addition to offering educational events like tree walks and talks, Tree Trust works with ISA-board-certified arborists committed to improving the health and longevity of mature trees. Protecting mature trees is essential to urban communities. Many are older than most community members, and these legacy trees offer immediate, irreplaceable benefits to our cities. Increased health and mental well-being, stormwater reduction, climate change mitigation, and economic benefits are all reasons to invest in big trees. One way Tree Trust does this is by welcoming the province to participate in the Ontario Tree Pageant. This engaging, inviting competition reminds the province that a love of trees goes far beyond the surface. For the past three years, hundreds of nominations have been received, special stories have been shared, and majestic trees have been recognized. This year’s esteemed panel of judges chose a tree that represents togetherness, a tree that is beloved and highlights a story of community awareness and environmental stewardship. This year’s winner is a Cucumber Tree ( Magnolia acuminata ), estimated to be over 100 years old, standing tall in St. George. This year’s winning tree was nominated by St. George resident and artist, Meredyth Kutt. This endangered, Ontario-native specimen stands among many other trees and is over 75 centimeters in diameter. Photo courtesy of Tree Trust . This tree is being recognized not only for being a unique and endangered species, but also for its history. Researchers at the University of Guelph have studied this individual for its ability to thrive outside its expected range. Some even say it is the farthest west mature Cucumber Tree in Canada. Beyond its uniqueness, this tree is celebrated as the epitome of environmental and community connection. The Kutt family, the tree’s owners, have stewarded it for over 20 years. They have cultivated a second Cucumber tree and currently support six of the original’s progeny. This cucumber tree’s story is exactly the kind of stewardship Tree Trust wants to support. The Ontario Tree Pageant gives people a platform to share special stories about trees that mean the most to them. It reminds us how connected we are to nature and that, for all these big trees give us, they deserve to be celebrated. The post Provincial Tree Pageant Reminds Communities to Honour Their Big Trees appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.description: Το Diwali είναι μια εποχή για να φωτίσουμε τα σπίτια μας με ντιγιά, αλλά το να γιορτάσουμε το φεστιβάλ βιώσιμα μπορεί να ξεκινήσει με κάτι τόσο χωρίς προβλήματα όπως η επαναχρησιμοποίηση αυτού που ήδη έχουμε. Αντί να αγοράζετε νέα χωμάτινα φωτιστικά κάθε χρόνο, λίγη δημιουργικότητα μπορεί να σας βοηθήσει να δώσετε στα παλιά diya μια νέα εμφάνιση. Η δημιουργός του lifestyle και των ταξιδιών Sharon JM Nathani, η οποία μοιράζεται ιδέες για DIY στο Instag…
items.descriptionOriginal: Diwali is a time to light up our homes with diyas , but celebrating the festival sustainably can begin with something as hassle-free as reusing what we already have. Instead of buying new earthen lamps every year, a little creativity can help give old diyas a fresh look. Lifestyle and travel creator Sharon JM Nathani, who shares DIY ideas on Instagram through her page @thatangloindiansindhi, suggests a simple way to reuse diyas from the previous year and make them ready for the festive season. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sharon JM Nathani || Lifestyle & Travel Creator (@thatangloindiansindhi) A trick to keep the wicks in place Her method involves using desi ghee and candles to prepare the diyas for lighting. She recommends heating the ghee, melting the candles into it, and pouring the mixture into the diyas before placing the wicks. This small change in the process makes a difference. Often, when the wicks are placed inside the diya before the liquid is poured, they can fall over or become crooked while filling. Sharon suggests pouring the mixture first and adding the wick afterwards, helping it stay upright and in place. Once the diyas are ready, you can add a little glitter or finely cut flower petals to decorate them. These small touches can give old lamps a festive makeover without the need to purchase new ones. Reusing diyas is an easy way to reduce waste during the festive season while making the most of items already at home. With a little effort, last year's lamps can return to your Diwali decorations, bringing the same festive warmth without adding to unnecessary consumption. This Diwali, before heading out to buy new decorations, take a look at what you already have. Sometimes, the most sustainable festive ideas begin with giving familiar things another chance.

items.title: Πώς ο «Artivism» οδηγεί την αντίσταση στο Παρίσι
items.titleOriginal: How ‘Artivism’ Is Driving the Resistance in Paris
items.description: Ξαφνικά ο Darth Vader ανεβαίνει σε μια καρέκλα μπροστά από το Hôtel de Ville στο Παρίσι. Ντυμένος στα μαύρα, κουνάει το σπαθί του σαν μαέστρος, ενώ 200 μουσικοί και εθελοντές, οι περισσότεροι γύρω στα είκοσι, ετοιμάζονται. Ξεπακετάρουν τα όργανά τους: βιολιά, τσέλο, κλαρίνα. Τότε ο πραγματικός μαέστρος, Étienne Jarrier, ανεβαίνει σε ένα πράσινο sh…
items.descriptionOriginal: S uddenly Darth Vader climbs up onto a chair in front of the Hôtel de Ville in Paris. Clad in all black, he swings his sword like a conductor’s baton while 200 musicians and volunteers, most in their early twenties, get ready. They unpack their instruments: violins, cellos, clarinets. Then the real conductor, Étienne Jarrier, steps up in a green shirt and the musicians of the Orchestre du Nouveau Monde (New World Orchestra) begin to play. Their song is a poignant one — El Pueblo Unido Jamás Será Vencido (The People United Will Never Be Defeated), a Chilean protest song written in the 1970s by the composer and pianist Sergio Ortega and folk group Quilapayún. It has since become an international hymn of resistance, and the members of the Orchestre du Nouveau Monde chant its refrain again and again to support the student protests in France this October, voicing their solidarity with the half million young people who are protesting high living costs and deteriorating conditions in their schools. “Music is a way for us to be heard,” says 25-year-old Jarrier, who co-founded the orchestra in 2022 “to find new ways forward.” A self-described “member of the climate generation,” the young man with the red-tinted black locks says he felt that climate activism had exhausted most avenues of protests and found it was time for “artivism,” art as a vehicle for political expression, “as a way of reaching people at the deepest level.” The post How ‘Artivism’ Is Driving the Resistance in Paris appeared first on Reasons to be Cheerful .

items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News PANORAMA Builds Replicable Conservation Solutions Database Spanning Nearly 1,900 Case Studies Worldwide Reading Time: 3 minutes A decade-old platform now hosts 1,897 conservation solutions from over 1,300 contributors, turning local environmental successes into replicable conservation solutions database entries anyone can adapt. For over ten years, PANORAMA – Solutions for a Healthy Planet has pursued a deceptively simple mission: build a global community where changemakers share, adopt, and scale up what already works. Rather than compiling passive success stories, this replicable conservation solutions database structures each entry as adaptable building blocks, distilling complex projects into stepwise blueprints practitioners elsewhere can actually apply to their own contexts. The scale is substantial. PANORAMA now hosts 1,897 documented solutions from 1,327 contributing organizations and individuals across 11 thematic communities spanning restoration, species conservation, marine and coastal ecosystems, One Health, protected areas under the 30×30 framework, and nature-culture heritage sites. This solutions database aligns explicitly with major global directives, including the Kunming-Montréal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Paris Agreement, and the UN’s 2030 Agenda, translating local action into evidence that supports international sustainability commitments. What distinguishes each entry within this replicable conservation solutions database is methodology rather than mere documentation. Every solution unpacks the how and why behind an effective environmental initiative, breaking successful projects into essential components others can adapt rather than simply admire. Solutions must be practical and tailored to specific scenarios, relevant to sustainability frameworks, proven through real-world results, and flexible enough for varied environments and sectors. Recent additions illustrate this approach in practice. In Mongolia, pastoral communities facing recurrent droughts and dzud , severe winter disasters causing catastrophic livestock losses, needed climate-resilient infrastructure. The UN Development Programme (UNDP) ADAPT Project responded by establishing 48 hay and feed storage facilities across four climate-vulnerable provinces, using risk assessments combining climate, vegetation, and livestock mortality data to identify optimal locations. The solution strengthened emergency fodder reserves while improving herders’ adaptive capacity against increasingly unpredictable seasons. Around Lake Victoria, shared by five East African nations and supporting over 45 million people through fisheries, water supply, and agriculture, declining water quality made coordinated basin management nearly impossible without shared evidence. The Lake Victoria Basin Commission, supported by GIZ, developed the first-ever State of the Basin Report, combining water quality sampling at 44 stations across three countries with consultations spanning all five partner states. This replicable conservation solutions database entry identifies wetland rehabilitation, reforestation, and catchment restoration as the most cost-effective pathways toward improved water quality, now serving as a shared baseline for planning across the entire basin. PANORAMA’s replicable conservation solutions database documents how five East African nations built a shared State of the Basin Report for Lake Victoria and how a multi-stakeholder partnership restored Ethiopia’s Lake Hawassa, both now scaled into national and regional policy frameworks. Photo by David Munyasa on Pexels. In Ethiopia’s Rift Valley, Lake Hawassa faced accelerating degradation from deforestation, pollution, erosion, and rapid urbanization, pressures no single actor could address alone. A multi-stakeholder partnership uniting public authorities, private companies, and civil society applied a Natural Resources Risk and Action Framework developed between 2015 and 2020, jointly assessing risks and implementing nature-based solutions. The partnership succeeded so thoroughly that it transitioned to full government management and scaled into federal guidelines, now restoring water bodies nationwide. This replicable conservation solutions database operates through a partnership network spanning 12 organizations, including GIZ, IUCN, UNDP, GRID-Arendal, UNEP, Rare, EcoHealth Alliance, ICCROM, the World Bank Group, OCTO Group, ICOMOS, and IFOAM. Together with over 1,000 individual solution providers representing institutions worldwide, this network forms the backbone connecting grassroots knowledge to global policy forums, ensuring diverse local perspectives genuinely influence international environmental decision-making rather than remaining isolated success stories. Peer-to-peer exchange sits at the platform’s core philosophy. Rather than treating conservation knowledge as proprietary or locked within academic journals, this replicable conservation solutions database transforms tacit, hard-won field experience into explicit, shareable wisdom. A coordinator from the Fiji Locally Managed Marine Area Network described the platform as compelling solution providers to examine their own work more critically, improving quality and scalability specifically because their solutions will be judged against a global standard for replicability. The database’s cross-cutting scope extends far beyond conservation biology alone. Communities addressing gender mainstreaming, financing mechanisms, governance structures, technology for nature conservation, and geodiversity all coexist within the same searchable platform, filterable by ecosystem type from agro-ecosystems to urban built environments, and by region spanning Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania, and the Coral Triangle. As climate and biodiversity crises intensify simultaneously, the pressure to avoid reinventing solutions grows correspondingly urgent. This replicable conservation solutions database offers exactly that efficiency: proven building blocks from Mongolian herders, East African basin commissions, and Ethiopian multi-stakeholder partnerships, structured so practitioners facing similar challenges elsewhere can adapt rather than start from zero, accelerating the pace at which local innovation becomes global practice. The post PANORAMA Builds Replicable Conservation Solutions Database Spanning Nearly 1,900 Case Studies Worldwide appeared first on Happy Eco News .

items.title: Ένας νομικός γραμματέας πήγε στο μετρό για να δουλέψει για 67 χρόνια. Κανείς δεν ήξερε ότι είχε 9 εκατομμύρια δολάρια.
items.titleOriginal: A Legal Secretary Rode the Subway to Work for 67 Years. Nobody Knew She had $9M.
items.description: Για 67 χρόνια, η Sylvia Bloom οδηγούσε το μετρό για τη δουλειά, ζούσε σε ένα διαμέρισμα που ελέγχεται από το ενοίκιο και περπάτησε μέσα από χιονοθύελλες στα 96 αντί να φτιάχνει ταξί -- όλα αυτά ενώ έχτιζε αθόρυβα μια περιουσία 9 εκατομμυρίων δολαρίων αντικατοπτρίζοντας τις μετοχές των αφεντικών της με μισθό γραμματέα. «Ήταν γραμματέας σε μια εποχή που έτρεχαν τη ζωή του αφεντικού τους, συμπεριλαμβανομένης της προσωπικής τους…
items.descriptionOriginal: For 67 years, Sylvia Bloom rode the subway to work, lived in a rent-controlled apartment, and walked through blizzards at 96 rather than hail a cab -- all while quietly building a $9 million fortune by mirroring her bosses' stock trades on a secretary's salary. "She was a secretary in an era when they ran their boss' lives, including their personal investments," her niece explained, and Bloom simply applied that same attentiveness to her own future, one modest purchase at a time. She never mentioned it to anyone - not colleagues, possibly not even her husband -- because, as her niece recalled, "she didn't think it was anybody's business but her own." What she did think was her business was what happened to it after she was gone: nearly all of it went to scholarships for students who couldn't afford college, becoming the largest individual gift in Henry Street Settlement's 125-year history. There is something clarifying about a life like hers -- the discipline kept private, the wealth worn invisibly, the generosity revealed only at the end, as if the whole thing had been a very long, very patient act of faith in someone else's future.
